explanation: Repeatedly splice the smaller head node onto the result. Once either list is exhausted, append the remaining suffix of the other list.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space; original nodes are reused.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: At each step, the smaller current head is no greater than any unconsumed node in either sorted list, so appending it preserves sortedness. Advancing only the selected list preserves every other node. When one list is exhausted, the other suffix is already sorted and can be appended unchanged. Each original node is included exactly once.
walkthrough: Merge [-3, 4, 9] and [-2, 4, 10]. Choose -3, then -2. At equal heads 4 and 4, take the first list’s 4, then the other 4. Finish with 9 and the remaining 10. Return [-3, -2, 4, 4, 9, 10].
edgeCases: Either or both input lists may be null.
Duplicates are preserved rather than coalesced.
Comparing values directly avoids subtraction overflow at integer extremes.
